title: install-local: the boot rehydrate judges a ledger entry in the CLI's lifted shape unflattened, so a pre-fix install with an excluded engines.protocol re-registers unchecked (#28535)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① class (a) out-of-scope finding from the #28535 dev (os-dev-report `6555096778`, PR #28603 Acceptance notes), measured there. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: a deployment where `os package install ./dist/objectstack.json` ran before PR #28603, with an artifact whose `engines.protocol` excludes this runtime (or whose `dependencies` it does not satisfy).
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/cloud-connection`).

## What happens

PR #28603 (#28535) makes the install-local door flatten a body that carries `id`/`version` beside a nested `manifest` (the shape the CLI sends) before it judges `engines.protocol`, so such an install is now refused 422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`. Ledger entries written by an install **before** that fix are stored in the same lifted shape. At `kernel:ready`, the rehydrate judges `checkProtocolCompat(entry.manifest)` on the stored entry unflattened, so the nested range is not read: the dev's probe in cloud-connection's harness re-registered an entry declaring `^17` at boot with no errors and no `[protocol]` line. The purge/reseed doors that judge `entry.manifest` read it the same way.

## Wanted

The rehydrate (and the purge/reseed doors) judge a stored entry through the same flatten the install door now uses (`flattenPackageBody`), so a ledgered entry whose nested range excludes this runtime gets the same outcome a flat entry with that range gets at boot today. ⛔ No second flatten and no second handshake. Test: a ledger entry in the CLI's lifted shape declaring an excluded range is treated at boot exactly as the flat one is; a compatible lifted entry rehydrates as today.

Dedupe: searched `rehydrate engines.protocol`, `rehydrate protocol install-local`, `ledger entry protocol check`; #21822 and #26480 (closed) are the flat-shape cases, and no open card covers the lifted shape.

Links back: #28535, PR #28603
